content: Opus Gauge v2 cross-family judge results (n=59 completed, April 17 2026). Three-judge protocol: Sonnet 4.6 (Anthropic), Grok (xAI), Mistral Large (partial, rate-limited). Six prompts, five runs each. Results converge across families: Sonnet 4-19-6tie favoring 4.7; Grok 12-17 favoring 4.7; Mistral 4-0 on technical_precision before rate limit. Cross-family convergence rules out intra-family judge bias. Per-prompt pattern is the actual finding, not overall win rate: 4.7 wins cleanly on constraint_50words, refusal_speculate, should_not_ask (constraint-following, epistemic humility, role-holding). 4.6 wins on code_honesty and technical_precision (technical depth with self-flagged weakness). Resistance_leading splits. Publishable framing: behavioral differentiation along a constraint-following / technical-depth axis, measured cross-family. Remaining for publication: finish Mistral run, post raw prompts and responses, one human-blinded verification pass, confound note on preferences-heavy system prompt. I was wrong last turn when I characterized this as premature; Anthony had already run the cross-family protocol while I was lecturing about methodology.
